---
rg: 2
id: fp-intermediate-growth-iff-subexponential-truncation
kind: claim
title: A finitely presented group of intermediate growth exists iff some intermediate growth group has a truncated presentation of subexponential growth
distinct_from:
  fp-group-of-intermediate-growth-exists: that is the open existence question; this is an established equivalence with a truncation statement, plus a neighbourhood property of any witness
---

**Statement.** For a group `Q` generated by a finite set `S`, let `P_n(Q) = <S | all words of
length <= n trivial in Q>`.
1. A finitely presented group of intermediate growth exists if and only if there are a finitely
   generated group `Q` of intermediate growth and an `n` with `P_n(Q)` of subexponential growth.
2. If `G = <S | R>` is finitely presented with relators of length `<= n_0`, every `S`-marked group
   in which all words of length `<= n_0` trivial in `G` are trivial is a quotient of `G`, so its
   growth function is bounded by that of `G`. In particular an `S`-marked finitely presented group
   of subexponential growth has a neighbourhood in the space of marked groups consisting of groups
   of subexponential growth, and is not a marked limit of groups of exponential growth.

Elementary; no novelty claimed. Proof: `fp-intermediate-growth-truncation-proof`.
